messages:
ashley: Quick heads up — we've got an incident impacting eu-db (increasing 5xxs). I'm pausing tonight's prod rollout. @deploybot please pin the current canary image and stop further rollouts.

deploybot: @ashley acknowledged. Pinning canary v2026.04.02-canary -> pinned. Cancelling queued deploys for prod window.

incident-bot: INCIDENT #2543 (eu-db-throttle) acknowledged by #oncall. Severity: P2. Current scope: read-heavy tails affecting model-serving routing. ETA initial triage 20m.

sam: Good call pausing. Can we avoid a full rollback? If we pin the canary and keep previous stable, we should be able to roll forward once the db circuit is mitigated.

ken: Agree — prefer staggered requeue instead of full rollback. If we rollback we need a db-migrations double-check. Suggest we block new releases and give ops 1 hour to confirm database state before reschedule.

marta: Noted. Need to confirm which kvcache/quantization PRs are in this canary. If those are sensitive, we should freeze model kernel changes until incident cleared.

ashley: Quick checklist I'm running through:
- pinned canary (deploybot) ✅
- cancelled prod queue ✅
- paused automated rollouts in all regions ✅
- notified customer-facing channels ✅
- ops triage assigned to @sam/@ken ✅

ashley: deploybot command used:
```
/deploy pin image=redwood/model:v2026.04.02-canary reason="incident pause eu-db-2543"
/deploy abort-queue env=prod reason="incident pause"
```

sam: Triage update: CPU pressure on primary read-replicas correlated with long tail queries from metric ingestion. Ops will apply a hotfix on the replica config (read_concurrency cap) and monitor for 15m. If error rate drops below 0.5% for 10m we can consider rescheduling.

ken: If hotfix stabilizes, proposal: reschedule to a short window (3am UTC) with strict canary ramp (5% -> 20% -> 100%) and manual hold between steps. No auto-promote.

marta: Also flagging: disable auto-quantize in runtime config for this canary until we validate perf after hotfix.

ashley: Agreed on manual hold. I'll update the rollout policy and add an explicit step to run smoke evals against prefix cache.

sara: I'll own the reschedule. Tentative new window Tue 03:00 UTC, 4h change window with canary-only first hour. Sending calendar invites and ops runbook update now. @ashley can you paste the updated rollout snippet you want in the release notes?

ashley: Paste for notes:
```
Rollout plan (post-incident):
1) 03:00 UTC - Start canary (5%), 15m hold + smoke evals
2) 03:20 UTC - Increase (20%), 15m hold + smoke evals
3) 03:40 UTC - Full promote (manual approval by ops)
Controls: auto-promote=false, quantize=false, kvcache-prefix-monitoring=on
Pinned fallback: stable@v2026.03.29
```

sara: Perfect. I'll add that to the release notes and mark the change window rescheduled. Also adding a note about the incident and playbook link.

deploybot: Calendar event created: "Prod rollout — rescheduled (Tue 03:00 UTC)". Pins: canary v2026.04.02-canary. Queue cleared.

ashley: Thanks all. Once sam/ken confirm the hotfix outcome, we'll reconvene here and either proceed with the new window or push further.

sam: Hotfix applied. Monitoring... error rate trending down, 10m moving avg at 0.42%. I'll confirm in 5m.

ken: If it holds, I'll be on the manual approve step for the 20->100% jump.

sam: Confirmed stable for 10m under 0.5%. Recommend proceed with staged reschedule per plan.

ashley: Proceed per plan. ops: manual hold at each step, no auto promote until stable for 15m.

sara: All updated in the release notes and calendar. I'll follow up with post-mortem link when available. :white_check_mark:

deploybot: Noted. Releases unblocked for scheduled window Tue 03:00 UTC with manual controls in place.

ashley: Closing thread for now. Re-open if regressions show up during the prep window.
